embeddings.title: Embeddings
embeddings.description: What turns memory, journals and knowledge into vectors, so agents find them by meaning. Voice message transcription always uses OpenAI with an API key.
embeddings.localHint: EmbeddingGemma, a multilingual model the worker runs on its own: free, nothing leaves your machine. Downloaded once, about 330 MB.
embeddings.ollamaHint: The same model (embeddinggemma) on your Ollama server, for example one with a GPU: free, and nothing leaves your machines.
embeddings.ollamaOff: To run the same model on an Ollama server instead, for example one with a GPU, turn Ollama on in <link>Settings > Models</link>.

readiness.localLoading: The worker is loading the built-in model (downloaded once, about 330 MB). Until it is ready, search matches by keyword.
readiness.localFailed: The worker could not load the built-in model. It tries again at the next embedding; check the worker logs if this stays.
readiness.ollamaUnreachable: Ollama does not answer at <mono>{url}</mono>. Start it, or change the address on the Ollama provider card.
readiness.ollamaModelMissing: Ollama answers, but the embedding model is missing. Pull it once: <mono>ollama pull embeddinggemma</mono>

embeddings.changeNotice: Saving clears the stored embeddings and embeds memory, journals and knowledge again with {provider}, in the background. Until then, search matches by keyword.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: What every agent is told, how much runs at once and the limits a new agent starts with.
agents.instructionsDescription: Goes into the system prompt of every agent: the super agent, project managers and specialists. Say who you are, the tone you want and the rules that always hold. Empty: nothing is added.
agents.instructionsPlaceholder: E.g. I run a small web agency. Keep answers short and direct. Never delete data without asking me first.
agents.delegationDescription: Tasks an agent hands to others from one conversation.
agents.parallelDelegationsHint: How many tasks delegated from one conversation run at the same time ({min}-{max}); the others wait and start on their own as these finish. Keep it low on a plan with a usage limit.
agents.limitsDescription: What a new agent starts with; each agent can change its own. Agents that exist keep theirs.
agents.maxStepsHint: How many steps (a model call and the tools it uses) a run may take before it stops.
agents.timeoutHint: A run still going after this long is stopped.
agents.budgetHint: Spend after which a run stops. Empty: no limit per run.
agents.maxRedelegationsHint: Times a delegated task can be sent back to be done again before you decide.
agents.maxFixRoundsHint: Automatic rounds of fixes a pull request gets for failed checks or review comments.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: What embeds memory, how much of it goes into each run and how long it stays.
memory.contextDescription: How much memory and journal an agent reads.
memory.pinnedTokensHint: Pinned entries go into the instructions of every run up to this size, newest first. While all the memory an agent can read fits, all of it goes in, pinned or not. About 4 characters per token.
memory.recallTokensHint: For each new message, the most relevant unpinned entries are added to it up to this size. 0 turns recall off.
memory.journalDaysHint: How many days of its own journal an agent reads at the start of each run (3-7 suggested).
memory.approvalDescription: Whether what agents remember on their own needs your review.
memory.requiresApproval: Memory written by agents needs approval
memory.requiresApprovalHint: Memories saved by agents stay pending until you approve them on the Memory page.
memory.ephemeralDaysHint: Days after which a memory saved as ephemeral expires.
memory.unusedDaysHint: Days without being recalled after which consolidation lists a memory for cleanup.

telegram.description: The bot you use to talk to the super agent: its token, who may use it and where notifications go.
telegram.botDescription: The token from @BotFather. Saving it restarts the bot, no worker restart needed.
telegram.tokenHint: Checked with Telegram when you save. Stored encrypted in Secrets as <mono>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</mono>.
telegram.tokenStored: Stored encrypted in Secrets, updated <time></time>. It is not shown again.
telegram.removeDescription: The bot stops at once: no Telegram messages or notifications until you save a token again.
telegram.tokenRemoved: Bot token deleted, the bot stopped
telegram.errorHint: Check the token, or stop any other program that uses this bot: Telegram allows only one to read its messages.
telegram.startingHint: The worker starts the bot in a few seconds. If this stays, check that the worker is running.
telegram.accessDescription: The bot answers only these users. Changes apply at once.
telegram.allowedUsersHint: Numeric Telegram user IDs, separated by commas. To find yours, message <mono>@userinfobot</mono>.
telegram.notifyChatHint: A user ID, or a group ID (negative, e.g. -1001234567890). Empty sends notifications to the first allowed user.
telegram.savedConnected: Saved. The bot @{username} starts in a few seconds.
telegram.commandsDescription: Set by the bot each time it starts: type / in the chat to see them.
telegram.secretDescription: Telegram bot token, set in Settings > Telegram

errors.tokenFormat: This does not look like a bot token. Copy the whole token from @BotFather, like 123456789:AA...
errors.tokenRefused: Telegram refused this token. Check that you copied it whole, or create a new one with @BotFather.
errors.unreachable: Telegram could not be reached to check the token. Try again in a moment.

telegram.topicsDescription: Projects with a telegramTopicId get their notifications in their own topic. The super agent answers messages written there, knowing which project the topic belongs to.
telegram.topicsEmpty: No project has a topic configured ({count, plural, one {# project} other {# projects}} in total). Set the topic ID on the project page.
telegram.step1: Open <mono>@BotFather</mono> in Telegram, send <mono>/newbot</mono> and paste the token it gives you in Bot token above.
telegram.step2: Save. The bot starts within a few seconds and its commands (listed above) are set automatically, no need for <mono>/setcommands</mono>.
telegram.step3: Add your Telegram user ID to Allowed users. To find it, message <mono>@userinfobot</mono>, or write to the bot in private: while you are not on the list, it replies with your ID.
telegram.step4: Optional, for notifications in a group: put the group ID in Notification chat. Left empty, notifications go to the private chat with the first allowed user.
telegram.step5: For one topic per project: create a group with Topics (forum) enabled, add the bot as an administrator, put the group ID in Notification chat, create a topic for each project and save the topic ID (message_thread_id, the last number in the link of a message from the topic) in the project settings.
telegram.transcriptionDescription: Voice messages are transcribed with OpenAI, so they need the OpenAI key.
